title: execution-manifest
description: The Slicr's output contract: a plan embeds one fenced JSON block {"execution-manifest": [entry, ...]}. The reference producer/validator is plan_to_nodes.py; an executor consumes the local:true entries as RED-gated nodes.

id.description: Node id; becomes the NN-<id>.json filename. Must be a path-safe slug: no path separators and no leading dot, so '..' and '.' are unrepresentable and the id can never traverse out of the output directory. The reference validator (plan_to_nodes.py) applies the same rule with re.fullmatch and is the authority where dialects differ on a trailing newline.

items.description: A repo-relative editable path. The pattern enforces the two rules a lookahead-free regex engine can express — no leading '/' and no leading '~' (which expanduser and shell tilde expansion resolve outside the repo). 'No .. component' still cannot be expressed here: it needs a negative lookahead, which the Rust regex crate does not support, so the reference validator remains authoritative. A producer trusting the schema alone can still emit a '..' path.

files.description: Editable files the node may change. Must be relative paths inside the repo: no leading '/', no '..' component. Enforced by the reference validator rather than by a pattern here — expressing 'no .. component' needs negative lookahead, which the Rust regex engine used elsewhere in this family does not support, and an unenforceable-by-some-consumers pattern is worse than a documented rule.

change.description: The task description shown to the executing model.

accept.description: Shell command; exit 0 iff the node is solved (the RED oracle).

kind.description: edit an existing region, or create a new single file.

forbid.description: Constraints the change must not violate.

local.description: Offload to an executor as a node. Only local:true entries become nodes; local:false is executed inline by the planning model.
